claim_scope: Research-only executable Tau evidence for observed/proof-carrying mutation. One contract models constitutional replacement candidates with an explicit predecessor, weakening residue proposal & predecessor', a fail-closed meet-ratchet that adopts equivalent/stronger proposals exactly and preserves predecessor obligations under weakening attempts, plus universal future-extension safety checks. A second contract proves append commutativity but exhibits restrict-then-extend noncommutativity and a concrete revoke/grant ordering dependency.
failure_modes: an equivalent or strengthening proposal is not adopted exactly by the meet-ratchet
a weakening proposal silently deletes predecessor obligations
the predecessor-to-proposal weakening residue is incorrectly zero for an unconstrained replacement
a future extension can admit settle=1 with a required proof or witness missing
the implementation assumes all table/state mutations commute
revoke-then-grant and grant-then-revoke are treated as the same final state
the replay runs against a mutable Tau source instead of the exact research lock

aaa.reason: The replay arranges equivalent, strengthening and weakening constitutional proposals plus concrete grant/revoke orderings; acts through Tau theorem queries and temporal ADT streams on the exact locked source; and asserts the full expected T/F sequence together with terminal stream states.

reject_is_noop.reason: The meet-ratchet turns the maximally weak proposal 1 into law[t]=law[t-1], demonstrating a fail-closed deletion attempt that preserves the predecessor. Identity restriction and empty extension are also explicit no-op boundaries.

boundary_dimensions.name: future_extension
points: proof core excludes missing proof for every x:tau
strengthened core excludes missing witness for every x:tau

boundary_dimensions.name: mutation_ordering
points: restrict/extend has an existential noncommutativity witness

nonclaims: This is a research-only logical experiment and grants no production, settlement, governance-execution, release, migration, verifier, or value-moving authority.
The meet-ratchet intentionally only permits equivalent-or-stronger evolution; it is not a complete constitutional amendment mechanism for explicitly authorized weakening.
A nonzero weakening residue classifies an unsafe replacement relative to the predecessor but is not by itself a cryptographic or consensus authorization.
The coordination classifier proves semantic order sensitivity; it does not implement distributed locking, consensus ordering, or a production scheduler.
The bounded examples use abstract Tau facts and fixed-width ids rather than production account, signature, hashing, or storage semantics.
This evidence does not close O-008 or refresh any pre-existing formal-cycle packet.
